races.name: Tote Guaranteed 50K Placepot Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: C Pas Possible
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old with a going profile that suits today; finished third over 2m4f at Galway on Good ground, so the course-and-going combination is a confirmed positive, and Daniel King is a competent handler, but the unknown style tag and just two career runs limit confidence.

runners_data.name: Dad Sez
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott who is training at a solid 3/35 strike rate over 14 days, but the horse's only form figure is a fall and his going profile is completely unknown — any assessment of his chance is essentially blind until he jumps off.

runners_data.name: De Jour En Jour
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a tidy placed record including three seconds and a third from six starts, and three of those came on Good ground, making today's conditions very familiar; handles 2m3f-plus well and Ross O'Sullivan's yard is quiet but this is a horse who consistently delivers on form.

runners_data.name: Eternal Reward
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse that fades in the finish — a combination that is structurally awkward over 2m6f on a sound surface today; returning after 297 days off and Danny Mullins' only form string shows a fall, so this is purely a speculative entry.

runners_data.name: Excessivebehaviour
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old returning after 248 days off who holds a fade flag in his profile — Mark Walsh cannot manufacture a run style the horse doesn't naturally own over this trip; the sole career start came on Heavy ground, making today's Good surface a complete unknown.

runners_data.name: Frankie's Freebie
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer who has placed five times in eight starts and finished second on Good ground recently, suggesting the surface and trip are within range; a seven-pound claimer takes the ride which reduces confidence, but the form profile is the most reliable in the lower-rated bracket.

runners_data.name: I Can Find Em
runners_data.note: The going profile is entirely unknown and the form string of 422 tails off — Mr O McGill carries an amateur claim but has had no visible platform to assess this horse's suitability to today's conditions or this trip.

runners_data.name: Jeroboam Machin
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who will set the pace today, and his Good-ground hurdle form includes two wins at shorter; the STYLE_FIT tag is relevant because he is stepping into a prominent role over 2m6f in a large field, which stretches his natural comfort zone, though his recent form (ran 19 days ago) suggests he is in condition.

runners_data.name: Killowen House
runners_data.note: Paul John Gilligan's horse has genuine placed form over course-relevant distances on Good ground, including a win, and arrives only 23 days fresh; by nature a hold-up horse, he finds himself pushed into the midfield pack in this 21-runner field — his best chance comes if the race develops into one he can still finish through rather than needing a true staying-on late burst.

runners_data.name: Kiltinan
runners_data.note: Just the one career run showing a fourth, and 241 days off since then — the going profile is unknown and the Alan O'Sullivan claim adds further uncertainty; hard to assess without a meaningful form line.

runners_data.name: Minella Post
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a patchy record including a fall and a pulled-up in recent starts; the five Good-ground runs average fifth place, which is underwhelming, and the hurdles headgear (t) combined with trainer Thomas Gibney's quiet 14-day record gives little confidence.

runners_data.name: Mr Erwitt
runners_data.note: Veteran of six Good-ground runs without a win or place, carrying a fade flag and a headgear note (tp); naturally a hold-up horse, he has been mapped to midfield simply because the rear is oversubscribed in this field — his form on this surface and his age (7) make it difficult to build a case for him contending.

runners_data.name: Mr Hollywood
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' hold-up horse has the most credible staying profile in the back half of the field — five career placings, and his 2m2f+ Good-ground record is better than the bare figures suggest; Brian Hayes rides and Mullins' yard is in the form of their lives, so if any hold-up horse can deliver from off the pace today, this is the one.

runners_data.name: Ol Parson
runners_data.note: The form string (P2-496) is contradictory and the two Good-ground runs both resulted in midfield finishes; the seven-pound claim from Conor Clarke softens the impact of 23 days' freshness but there is nothing in the evidence to identify this horse as a live contender today.

runners_data.name: Rumi Rock
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up horse who has run twice on Good ground with placings of sixth and tenth — uninspiring, and the fade tag compounds the concern; Phillip Enright has recent contact (ran 8 days ago) which is a mild positive, but the form profile offers no traction.

runners_data.name: Tom Mac
runners_data.note: Just a single career run — sixth over 2m3f on Good ground 114 days ago — giving almost nothing to evaluate; the unknown style tag and Paul O'Flynn's quiet yard mean this is a watch-and-learn entry rather than a live market mover.

runners_data.name: Trotters Traders
runners_data.note: Ran once, finished 16th of 17 on Good ground 19 days ago over a shorter trip — the form is unambiguous and the fade flag means this trip extension is unlikely to help; Paul John Gilligan runs three today which dilutes stable focus.

runners_data.name: Trev The Rev
runners_data.note: The youngest horse in the field at four, returning after 120 days and with the lightest weight at 161lbs; the sole run came on Soft and the style and going are unknown — too many questions to identify a clear angle.

runners_data.name: Al Arrivee
runners_data.note: Two wins and three places from five career starts, two of those wins on Good ground at 2m and 2m2f — the form profile is the strongest in the race and the step up to 2m6f is the main question; Patrick Mullins takes the ride for his father's operation which is rolling at 5/26 over 14 days, and this horse carries a clear profile advantage for the dominant race shape today.

runners_data.name: Shoda
runners_data.note: JJ Slevin partners this JP O'Brien-trained five-year-old who has a win on Soft and placed form on Good — the operation is in outstanding form at 19/68 over 14 days; the prominent style suits tracking the pace, though the 148-day break and a form string that tails off to a dash is a concern at the longer trip.

runners_data.name: Walkingmayotomilan
runners_data.note: Returning after 185 days with a fade flag and a form string ending in a pulled-up — the hold-up profile over 2m6f on Good ground without a jockey named is alarming; the evidence points firmly against.

races.paceDynamic: Jeroboam Machin is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 21-runner maiden hurdle over 2m6f on Good ground at Galway, and with no other genuine pace horse likely to press him, he should be allowed to dictate at a comfortable, sustainable tempo from the front. Al Arrivee and De Jour En Jour will push forward into prominent positions just off the leader, with Shoda and Frankie's Freebie also likely to sit handily, creating a bunched prominent group rather than a strung-out procession. The true hold-up horses Mr Hollywood, Rumi Rock, Killowen House, and Mr Erwitt will be forced to race further back than ideal, but Killowen House and Mr Erwitt are redistributed from the rear — they are natural hold-up types who cannot claim that position in this 21-runner field and will race in midfield against their instincts, discounting their prospects in any late-closer scenario. A genuine go-to-post pace with one uncontested leader on Good ground over a searching 2m6f trip at Galway strongly favours prominent racers who can track the pace from the second fence, conserve energy in a well-organised rhythm, and produce a sustained challenge from 3 out — hold-up horses who need a strong end-to-end gallop to launch from are at a structural disadvantage today.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Jeroboam Machin sets a controlled pace and prominent trackers travel smoothly before asserting from 3 out.
scenarios.body: Jeroboam Machin dictates at a moderate gallop, allowing Al Arrivee and De Jour En Jour to stalk him in the first two, with the race effectively run between this group from the home turn; Al Arrivee's two course wins over similar Good ground and Willie Mullins' yard firing in fine form make him the archetype beneficiary, while De Jour En Jour's consistent placed form also suits a tracking role on this surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Jeroboam Machin is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the moderate tempo means the field never quite reels him in.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to test Jeroboam Machin early, he conserves energy at his own pace and simply proves too far gone by the time the closers mount a challenge in the straight; his Good-ground form is acceptable and trainer Emmet Mullins sends him here in form, though the STYLE_FIT tag and the step up in field size are genuine questions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fast enough to soften the prominent horses and genuine closers find daylight through a tiring field in the straight.
scenarios.body: Mr Hollywood has the class pedigree under Willie Mullins and has placed in five of his last five starts, making him the most dangerous late runner if conditions set up right; however, Killowen House and Mr Erwitt are redistributed from their true hold-up role and are unlikely to deliver the sustained late momentum their profile would require, limiting the depth of this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the race fragments and an unexposed or lightly-raced runner surfaces at a big price under a confident conditional ride.
scenarios.body: This field contains several lightly-raced and unknown quantities — Kiltinan, Tom Mac, Dad Sez, and I Can Find Em carry UNKNOWN going profiles and have minimal form to anchor, meaning one could outrun expectations in a chaotic 21-runner maiden; this scenario is low probability but non-trivial given the maiden status, the size of the field, and the number of horses with a single career run.

watchPoints.text: Al Arrivee carries the strongest form profile in the field — two wins on Good ground, Willie Mullins' yard in top form, and a running style that directly fits the prominent-stalker scenario — watch him closely from the second fence as the default race-shape beneficiary.

Mr Hollywood is the hold-up horse with the most credible staying pedigree in the back half of the field under Brian Hayes for Willie Mullins; if the pace quickens enough to soften the prominent group, he is the most dangerous late threat, but watch whether he gets a clear run in a 21-runner field.

Jeroboam Machin sets the tempo for the entire race — if he is allowed to dictate unchallenged at a comfortable clip, the race could be over as a contest before the home turn; watch his jumping and his lead margin at halfway.

Dad Sez is entirely unexposed under Jack Kennedy for Gordon Elliott — an operation capable of producing a ready-made winner first time out; the complete absence of form makes him a watch-for-market-moves runner rather than an assessable form pick.

Shoda for JP O'Brien and JJ Slevin merits monitoring on market moves given the yard's 14-day strike rate of 19/68 — the 148-day absence is the key flag, but if the market moves for this one it likely reflects

races.name: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Hees Dynamite
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who can coast along in front on Good ground over her preferred trip; T14 strike rate 1/14 is modest and racing at the top of her OR, but uncontested lead makes her dangerous to dismiss entirely even if STYLE_FIT suggests this is not her optimum setup.

runners_data.name: Harbour Highway
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden in the saddle for Emmet Mullins (T14 1/7) is a strong booking angle; hold-up style suits this scenario perfectly, goes well on Good ground (9/15 similar-going), and Galway's undulating track over 2m6f plays to his staying profile.

runners_data.name: Mephisto
runners_data.note: Has run 12 of 15 on similar going and boasts a solid strike rate for Gerard Keane (T14 1/4); naturally prominent but does have a tendency to fade (form 15P-47) and the visor may be needed to sharpen his finish.

runners_data.name: Oneforgonzo
runners_data.note: Won over 2m on Good at Galway and showed prominently there; 69 days off is a query but the form includes a recent win and a second, and a 7lb claimer on board keeps weight competitive — one of the prominent types most likely to actually secure a forward position.

runners_data.name: Granville Street
runners_data.note: Shorter-trip specialist stepping up markedly in distance (best form over 12-14f); Good-ground form is there but 2m6f at Galway looks a stamina stretch and the recent form has been moderate (P670).

runners_data.name: Ollie La Ba Ba
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie applied; prominent racer whose Good-ground record is solid (11/15) but whose form is stubbornly consistent without threatening to win at this level — six runs without a top-three finish in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Camino Rock
runners_data.note: 188 days off the track is a major fitness concern; form since returning to Good ground has been poor (9s and Ps), and a 7lb apprentice on a hold-up horse who hasn't run since February asks significant questions.

runners_data.name: Coded Welder
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie; promising Good-ground profile (7/9 similar going) and two recent placings including a second last month suggest fitness is good; prominent style but tends to finish without winning, suggesting he needs an unusually strong pace to pounce.

runners_data.name: Golden Temple
runners_data.note: Won five days ago (LR:5d) for Noel Meade (T14 3/13 — notable form trainer) — quick turnaround but clearly in form; hold-up type who won over 2m on Good at Galway last time; the tongue-tie and bit help him settle and the trip extension to 2m6f looks manageable.

runners_data.name: I'll Be Handy
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in finish — a concern over 2m6f; form shows repeated seconds and a fifth, indicating he places without winning; hold-up style but the staying-on issue makes this trip a worry, and 68 days off adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Lord Ffrench
runners_data.note: Consistent Good-ground hold-up type (9/11 similar going) with a win to his name; six runs without a top-two finish recently but this trip and going combination suits and Phillip Enright is an experienced partner — quietly interesting at big odds.

runners_data.name: Imarajan
runners_data.note: Won over 1m10f on Good at Galway recently and placed in follow-up; 5-year-old on the upgrade for Eoin Doyle (T14 1/5) with a 7lb claimer; prominent style and solid Good-ground record (9/13) make him one to watch closely near the front.

runners_data.name: Andys Flame
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner by nature, but with 24 horses chasing early positions, this 9-year-old veteran is likely to find himself further back than ideal; John McConnell (T14 0/24) has had a quiet fortnight and the redistribution means pace fitness is the key variable.

runners_data.name: Cornmarket
runners_data.note: Two wins over 2m6f at Galway on Good make him fascinatingly course-and-distance qualified; his natural racing style is up with the pace, which this map has him unable to express — if he does find rail room early, his track record here is formidable.

runners_data.name: Paul Collins
runners_data.note: Placed last time (3rd over 2m4f on Good for Brian McMahon, T14 1/4); prominent type with solid Good-ground stats (11/15) but the form also includes a string of zeros and a P, so consistency is a concern even if the recent run was encouraging.

runners_data.name: Tangara Bay
runners_data.note: Won most recently (1st over 1m11f on Soft) but returns from 125 days off and has only one Good-ground run in the last five (no wins); Peter Fahey yard (T14 1/9) is ticking over, but the going and trip combination is untested at this level.

runners_data.name: Lucy Wang
runners_data.note: Won over 2m4f on Good at Galway and placed multiple times for Emmet Mullins (T14 1/7); a natural up-with-the-pace type who the map has pushed back given field size — 114 days off is a concern but Mullins horses often return fresh, and the course form is compelling.

runners_data.name: Mighty Berkshire
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 59 days off; form figures are moderate (4th last time) and Good-ground stats are limited (5/7 similar going); owner-trainer combo and amateur jockey suggest stable confidence may not be high.

runners_data.name: Therellbguddaysyet
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old veteran whose natural style is prominent but who, in a 23-runner field, will struggle to express it; Paul O'Flynn (T14 0/0) quiet; recent form (58P) raises questions about current ability at this level regardless of positioning.

runners_data.name: Macshadow Des Crai
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy is a significant jockey booking for a 4-year-old (unusual at this age for a hurdle handicap) who has placed twice including a second on Soft — 122 days off and limited Good-ground form (1/4 similar) are queries, but the Kennedy ride demands respect.

runners_data.name: Clonbury Bridge
runners_data.note: Has run 13 of 15 on similar going — the most durable Good-ground profile in the field — and placed at 2m on Good; a natural front-runner who, over 2m6f in a packed field, will likely find himself more rearward than suits, though the trip and going are ideal.

runners_data.name: Priory Park
runners_data.note: 10-year-old veteran whose recent form (504P9) is discouraging; 102 days off and no jockey listed publicly; a natural prominent type now mapped further back — the combination of age, form, and positional disadvantage makes this a difficult ask.

runners_data.name: Mavetherave
runners_data.note: Second over 2m2f on Good last time out for Claire O'Connell is a positive; naturally prominent but redistributed given the crowded front — limited Good-ground stats (4/9) and modest OR make winning hard to envisage unless she secures a forward pitch.

races.paceDynamic: Hees Dynamite is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine pressure for the lead — she can dictate a comfortable, even gallop over 2m6f on Good ground at Galway without being harassed. Behind her, a cluster of natural prominent racers including Cornmarket, Andys Flame, Therellbguddaysyet, Lucy Wang, Clonbury Bridge, Priory Park, and Mavetherave are redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds far more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position; in a 23-runner handicap hurdle, Oneforgonzo, Imarajan, and Mephisto are best placed among the prominent types to actually force their way into early contention behind Hees Dynamite. The resulting race shape is a controlled, single-file procession at a sustainable pace, which means stamina will be tested over the final half-mile but the early gallop will not have burnt off the hold-up horses prematurely. This race shape decisively favours genuine hold-up horses who settle well, travel powerfully in the second half of the race, and have the stamina for 2m6f — closers with proven Good-ground form get the clearest run through a tiring field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Hees Dynamite sets a sustainable gallop unchallenged and the prominent scrimmage burns out the redistributed types.
scenarios.body: Hees Dynamite dictates an honest but unforced tempo, and the hold-up horses travel comfortably before unleashing sustained finishes from the second-last; 2m6f on Good ground rewards those who have settled and conserved energy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine prominent stayers Oneforgonzo, Imarajan, and Mephisto successfully press Hees Dynamite and convert early momentum into victory.
scenarios.body: A slightly more contested pace develops as several prominent types clamour for position in a 23-runner field, but the stamina of front-rank runners who settle just off the lead proves decisive; Oneforgonzo and Imarajan have the Good-ground form and trip credentials to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough in the middle stages to create a true stamina test that suits a late, deep closer.
scenarios.body: Macshadow Des Crai or Lord Ffrench, racing well off the pace and conserving energy, pick off tiring horses from the final flight with a strong staying finish; this scenario requires a more pressured gallop than Hees Dynamite alone is likely to generate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Breaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If one of the mapped-midfield runners who is truly prominent in nature — Cornmarket or Andys Flame — wrestles a front-rank position early and converts class.
scenarios.body: In a large, scrimmaging field, an experienced prominent type who finds the rail or a gap could steal into a prime position and outstay rivals in the final quarter-mile; Cornmarket's two wins over 2m6f at Galway make it the most credible beneficiary of this low-probability shape.

watchPoints.text: Golden Temple has won five days ago for the in-form Noel Meade yard (T14 3/13) and arrives fit, course-proven, and with the hold-up profile perfectly suited to a single-pacemaker scenario — watch for him travelling ominously into contention from the second-last.

Harbour Highway (Harry Cobden, Emmet Mullins) is a classic big-field hold-up horse on Good ground — watch for Cobden tracking the pace from the rear before delivering a strong challenge at the final flight.

Imarajan is one of the few prominent types with a realistic chance of actually securing a front-rank position behind Hees Dynamite — watch his early positioning; if he tracks the leader cleanly, his recent Galway form and upward trajectory make him a live threat.

Cornmarket's two wins over this exact course and distance on Good are impossible to ignore — if he finds a position near the pace despite the redistribution concern, his course record alone makes him dangerous and he should be tracked carefully from the outset.

With 23 runners and a cluster of natural front-runners forced back into midfield, the early stages at Galway's tight track could see significant positional scrimmaging — horses drawn wide or with inexperienced riders (multiple 7lb claimers in the field) may struggle to slot in, creating interference risk at the early hurdles

races.name: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: She's A Fine Wine
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with excellent Good-ground form (4W 6P in similar conditions), gets to bowl along uncontested which suits, but the STYLE_FIT tag notes she is rated as a prominent type here — her chance is highest if she is simply allowed to control this race from the front unchallenged.

runners_data.name: Venusienne
runners_data.note: Mullins-Cobden combination is always significant at Galway; went 1-2 in last two Good-ground starts and the 2m½f trip looks ideal; naturally prominent and capable of holding a forward position even in this field.

runners_data.name: Missus Beeton
runners_data.note: Best form comes on Soft going (two wins) and the sim-going stats show concern on Good (1W5P); prominent racer who needs to be in the first three jumping, but the Going is against her absolute best.

runners_data.name: Billie Frechette
runners_data.note: Dual Good-ground winner at 2m2f-2m6f and the trip suits well; naturally prominent and Noel Meade in good current form; three-runner sample on this trip limits certainty but the profile fits the likely race shape well.

runners_data.name: Samba Train
runners_data.note: Three wins on Good ground from seven starts and the form-string ending in a win last time is encouraging; naturally front-running but the 7lb claim from Halford may matter less on a flat track — likely to be one of the horses who does get a forward position.

runners_data.name: Ardeen Joy
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy booking is a major flag in a competitive handicap; won last time on Good ground over 2m4f and the trip up to 2m½f looks workable; genuine prominent racer who should comfortably secure a position near the pace in running.

runners_data.name: Splashing Out
runners_data.note: One of the truest hold-up horses in the race, winning twice on Good ground; Peter Smithers's claim takes weight off but this is a competitive field — if congestion develops in the prominent group, Splashing Out is the horse most naturally positioned to benefit.

runners_data.name: Zahra Dodville
runners_data.note: Sole Good-ground win in four hurdle starts, so sample is limited; natural front-runner but the 5lb claim from Hogan is useful — though heavily surrounded by other prominent types, she may struggle to find her preferred position.

runners_data.name: Camlin Park
runners_data.note: Returned from 114-day break and had two pulled-up runs before a 2m2f win on Good ground; likely to face fitness questions after a long absence and inconsistent recent form limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Fratas
runners_data.note: J J Slevin is a significant jockey booking for the Joseph O'Brien yard; genuine hold-up performer who may be best served by a messy race — the small sim-going sample (1W4P) is not alarming given the natural style suits a tactical scenario.

runners_data.name: Wonderfulwonderful
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground and is lightly raced at four, suggesting potential for improvement; naturally prominent but is one of many such types here — likely to be pushed back from her preferred position in a 23-runner field.

runners_data.name: Crohan Lady
runners_data.note: Won last time at shorter and has Good-ground form at 2m4f, which is a legitimate angle; a natural front-runner who will find herself mapped further back than ideal given the overcrowded prominent group — that positional compromise is the key risk.

runners_data.name: Cleopatra's Needle
runners_data.note: Went 2-2 in recent starts on Good and Soft ground; a true prominent racer whose natural habit is to race close to the pace, but with so many similar types here she is likely to be forced to race without cover — that displacement matters.

runners_data.name: Hillhead Runner
runners_data.note: Recent form has regressed (4-7-9-8-2) and the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 1/6 is modest; wants to race prominently but Good-going form is extensive (12 from 12 sim-going runs) — form is there in principle but the declining sequence is a concern.

runners_data.name: Two Pair
runners_data.note: Won at 2m1f on Good ground and has a consistent profile; another natural front-runner reassigned to midfield by race shape — the lack of an able jockey booking here makes it harder to see how it overcomes positional disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Simple Things
runners_data.note: Has been placed twice in recent Good-ground runs at 2m4f and the Dempsey yard angle is worth noting; a horse whose genuine nature is to race prominently but will find itself in midfield — the form over this trip and going is the best thing about it.

runners_data.name: Astelia
runners_data.note: Has placed second in three consecutive runs, all on Good ground — a mare arriving in peak form but yet to win over this trip; despite being reassigned from its natural prominent role, consistent finishing suggests it could still run into a place.

runners_data.name: Bossy Bird
runners_data.note: Tagged with a fade-in-finish warning, which is a notable concern in a race over 2m½f on Good ground; a prominent type shifted back by field size, and the combination of style displacement and tendency to tire late is doubly negative.

runners_data.name: Small Bucks
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer who won last time (2m2f, Good) and has solid sim-going stats; the fade-in-finish flag is a concern over this slightly longer trip — one of a small group of true hold-up horses whose position is not artificially mapped.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Doubt
runners_data.note: Ran just yesterday (1-day LR), which is a major fitness and freshness query in a handicap of this class; a natural prominent runner who loses positional advantage and is effectively appearing under significant physical stress from a near-consecutive run.

runners_data.name: Emesteraye
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with two recent thirds on Good ground and consistent recent form; no jockey listed in the data which creates uncertainty, but the style is genuine and the trip is slightly longer than recent wins — place potential in the right scenario.

runners_data.name: Tingarran Express
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with consistent Good-ground form but recent record shows a drop in form (9th last time); a front-runner by nature who will be unable to obtain that role here — age combined with positional compromise makes this a difficult win chance.

runners_data.name: You Make Me Smile
runners_data.note: Good-ground placed form is solid and recent, going 2-3-2 in last three on similar going; a true prominent type who will race behind its ideal position in this field — the consistent finishing effort in good conditions is the most relevant positive.

races.paceDynamic: She's A Fine Wine is the one confirmed front-runner in this 23-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing or able to press her at the head of affairs, she is set to control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop over 2m½f on Good ground at Galway. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which historically at this track and trip compresses the field and keeps things together until the final climb, when finishing quality and jumping accuracy over the last two flights become decisive. Venusienne, Billie Frechette, Ardeen Joy, and Samba Train are the prominent types most capable of actually securing a position close to the pace, with the remainder of the apparent prominent brigade — Crohan Lady, Cleopatra's Needle, Simple Things, Hillhead Runner, Two Pair, Astelia, Bossy Bird, Sea Of Doubt, Tingarran Express, and You Make Me Smile — all natural front or prominent runners who cannot all occupy that space and will be pushed further back than they want. The resulting traffic and positional friction through the body of the field means the tactical verdict favours genuine prominent performers who travel fluently in the first half-dozen and can quicken from a stalking position once She's A Fine Wine's controlled pace inevitably quickens the tempo entering the home straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If She's A Fine Wine dictates an honest but unhurried gallop and the closest prominent movers strike turning for home.
scenarios.body: She's A Fine Wine sets a sustainable tempo that keeps the race together, and horses travelling prominently in second to sixth wheel off the final bend with energy in reserve; the Galway finish rewards those who have saved ground and jump the last two hurdles cleanly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop remains genuinely moderate and She's A Fine Wine is never seriously challenged, allowing her to coast home on the bridle.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied from flagfall, She's A Fine Wine could simply be unmatchable on energy conservation alone, her Good-ground form reading 4W6P in similar conditions; the prominent chasers arrive too late as the leader has stolen an untouchable rhythm.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Congestion Chaos, Hold-Up Reward
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded prominent group causes interference and the pace collapses in the straight, leaving late runners to mop up.
scenarios.body: The glut of natural front-runners pushed against their will into midfield creates choking traffic through the body of the race, and genuine hold-up performers who bypass the scrimmage emerge with momentum at the death; Splashing Out and Fratas are the truest hold-up profiles who benefit if the pace implodes.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Mover Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If a lightly-raced or underrated type tracks the pace without cover and quickens past beaten rivals from two out.
scenarios.body: With 23 runners on Good ground, a single horse can thread through a gap and catch everything flat-footed if positioned wide of traffic; Zahra Dodville or Simple Things, despite redistribution pressure, could benefit if the right channel opens.

watchPoints.text: Sea Of Doubt ran just one day ago and connections must be monitored for a late withdrawal — if it runs, it carries a serious fitness risk and could compromise horses around it in a 23-runner field.

The overcrowded prominent group — including Crohan Lady, Cleopatra's Needle, Hillhead Runner, Simple Things, Two Pair, Bossy Bird, Astelia, Tingarran Express, Sea Of Doubt, and You Make Me Smile — all want to be close to the pace; watch for early positional scrimmaging and potential interference at the first two hurdles in a 23-runner cavalry charge.
Bossy Bird and Small Bucks both carry fade-in-finish flags over a trip of 2m½f on Good ground — if either is in contention at the final hurdle, they are likely to weaken on the run-in.

She's A Fine Wine is the sole confirmed front-runner and if she makes an error at any stage the entire race dynamic changes abruptly; any hesitation from her at the early hurdles could trigger a pace collapse and turn the race into a sprint finish from the home bend.

Jack Kennedy's booking for Ardeen Joy stands out as a market indicator — monitor any significant market move in the hour before the off, as Kennedy rarely takes competitive festival rides without strong expectation.

races.name: Tote Galway Plate (Handicap Steeplechase) (Grade 3)

runners_data.name: Senecia
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a win on Good over similar trips; 79 days off, blinkered, and Mr J C Barry handles him well — sits close to pace and stays every yard of 2m6½f.

runners_data.name: Three Card Brag
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner and the key pace influence in this race; Kevin Healy's 7lb claim helps, Good form is adequate, but winning from the front in a 25-runner handicap chase is a tall order despite controlling the tempo.

runners_data.name: Funiculi Funicula
runners_data.note: Paul Townend's mount is a natural prominent type with a fine Good-ground record and recent wins at shorter; this is his chase debut season's stamina test and the 2m6½f is at the outer limit of his current proven range.

runners_data.name: Gorgeous Tom
runners_data.note: Good-ground record is solid (8 wins/places from 15 similar runs) and he races close to the pace, but recent form has been modest and De Bromhead's yard is in fine shape — the fifth-highest OR in the field.

runners_data.name: Will The Wise
runners_data.note: Tongue tie and a strong Good-ground profile (six runs, one win, four places); prominent style suits a controlled pace and Donoghue is an astute pilot for a race like this — 110 days off is the one flag.

runners_data.name: Jesse Evans
runners_data.note: Exceptional going profile — 15 from 15 runs on Good ground producing four wins and eleven placed efforts; prominent style and a 58-day break keeps him fresh for a race that suits every angle of his profile.

runners_data.name: Ol Man Dingle
runners_data.note: Won last time on Good at 20f with tongue-tie and a prominent style; stepping up to 2m6½f is the query but he arrives on a 44-day turnaround in form, and Griffin has placed him well all season.

runners_data.name: Perceval Legallois
runners_data.note: Cobden takes the ride and the horse ran 19 days ago; prominent type with a tongue tie and a recent 2nd at this trip on Good — consistent but lightly exposed at this level.

runners_data.name: Downmexicoway
runners_data.note: Good-ground form figures show 2 wins from 6 comparable runs; prominent racer who has been off 141 days, which is the longest break in the field and is a meaningful concern for match fitness.

runners_data.name: Rocky's Diamond
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a tongue tie, young (6yo), and only a modest Good-ground record (2W4P from 14 runs); apprentice Kenneally faces a big ask in a 25-runner Grade 3.

runners_data.name: Nowwhatdoyouthink
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy aboard a horse who is 3W6P from 10 Good-ground runs — an outstanding profile; prominent, tongue-tied, and placed at this trip before, he arrives fresh on 92 days.

runners_data.name: Reverend Hubert
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who is in outstanding recent form (1-1-5-1 from last four Good runs), 14 from 15 on Good overall; 19 days is a quick turnaround but Byrnes runs horses to win fresh.

runners_data.name: Maxxum
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer with a flat recent run (10th at Galway on Good); carries [STYLE_FIT] flag as he will struggle to get his usual position in this traffic — his chance depends on a pace shape he is unlikely to control.

runners_data.name: Nouvotic
runners_data.note: Four wins from nine Good-ground runs and a dynamic recent record; but as a true prominent type displaced to midfield by the volume of pace-horses, he is likely to race outside his comfort zone unless he can force his way forward early.

runners_data.name: Buddy One
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has not won on Good in this company and runs off 21 days; form has dipped (6-6-P-4-0) and the demanding 2m6½f trip is further than his best.

runners_data.name: King Alexander
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained prominent type who must race in midfield given the crowded pace picture; his Good record is decent (2W3P from 7) but a [STYLE_FIT] concern applies and Daniel King faces a tactical puzzle with 25 runners.

runners_data.name: King Of Kingsfield
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who wears a tongue-tie and hood, and who finished only fifth 27 days ago; apprentice Halford has a 7lb claim but the horse's Good-ground chase form is mixed.

runners_data.name: Spread Boss Ted
runners_data.note: Mullins yard in fine form, but this horse is a natural prominent type who cannot hold that berth in this field; his three Good-ground runs produced only one win and limited placed effort, limiting confidence even if Brian Hayes negotiates the traffic.

runners_data.name: Solitary Man
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip on Good at 26f last time and carries a strong Good-ground profile (4W7P from 15); though displaced to midfield, he is a naturally prominent horse who will want to get forward — his recent win suggests he is in top form.

runners_data.name: Ballygunner Castle
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the ride and the horse shows two placings on Good at 20f; a natural front-runner bumped back in the map, he will find it difficult to express his jumping style with 25 rivals in a competitive handicap.

runners_data.name: Barry Lyndon
runners_data.note: Won on Good at 24f last time and has a 3W4P record on similar going; a true prominent type mapped to midfield because of field size — Slevin is an excellent jockey but the positional squeeze is a genuine concern.

runners_data.name: Conyers Hill
runners_data.note: Recent back-to-back seconds on Good suggest he is in form; his natural prominent style is compressed into midfield, which is a tactical difficulty, though he handles the course profile and the 24f trip.

runners_data.name: Jalila Moriviere
runners_data.note: Two recent seconds on Good at 20f are encouraging; tongue-tied and a true prominent type who will likely sit deeper than ideal — no jockey listed which is a flag, and improvement needed at this OR.

runners_data.name: Boston Rover
runners_data.note: Three wins in four completed runs on Good ground, making his going profile the most compelling in the field; but he ran only 19 days ago, is a natural prominent type who cannot get that position here, and drops from hurdles context.

runners_data.name: Ballybawn Belter
runners_data.note: No wins on Good from eight attempts and best form has been on Soft or Heavy; a natural prominent type who will not get close to the pace here, making his task even harder in a race where the going plays to his weakness.

races.paceDynamic: Three Card Brag is the lone confirmed front-runner and, critically, is unlikely to be seriously pressured for the lead in this 25-runner field — he sets a sustainable, controlled tempo around Galway's tight, undulating circuit and essentially dictates terms from flag to finish. The genuine pace in this race is denser than it first appears: Nouvotic, Maxxum, Spread Boss Ted, Solitary Man, King Alexander, Barry Lyndon, Ballygunner Castle, Conyers Hill, Jalila Moriviere, Boston Rover and Ballybawn Belter are all natural prominent types who cannot all hold that position and have been mapped to midfield as a result — of these, Senecia, Will The Wise, Jesse Evans, Funiculi Funicula and Gorgeous Tom are the most likely to actually press forward and sit closest to Three Card Brag. With a solo leader drip-feeding the pace, the race will develop into a prolonged stamina test over the final mile, rewarding those settled comfortably in the first half-dozen who travel without burning fuel early. A controlled, galloping tempo on Good ground over 2m6½f at Galway — a right-handed, sharp track that places a premium on jumping fluency and stamina rather than a closing burst — most strongly favours prominent racers with genuine Good-ground form and a clean jumper's profile rather than true hold-up horses attempting to make up ground late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Three Card Brag sustains a steady tempo and the main contenders settle just off the pace without incident, preserving their energy for the final two fences.
scenarios.body: The race unfolds at an even gallop with the front rank well-organised, allowing prominent horses with strong Good-ground records to produce a measured staying effort; the final bend and run-in filters for jumping accuracy and stamina over raw speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Three Card Brag is allowed to dictate completely unchallenged, sets a frugal pace and produces a jumping display that leaves rivals unable to close.
scenarios.body: With 25 runners bunching and losing momentum at obstacles, the leader's clean round at a solo tempo means rivals never get close enough to peg him back turning in; a front-runner's dream scenario on a sharp track.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stayer Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is slightly stronger than expected and the prominent brigade empty their tanks, allowing redistributed hold-up types to stay on past tired rivals on the run-in.
scenarios.body: With energy spent upfront and the field stringing out after the fourth-last, genuine stayers who were held up or carried wider carry their momentum deep into the race; Good ground and a true stamina test is essential.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Explosion, Holds-Up Win
scenarios.trigger: If crowding and early barging cause a faster-than-expected split early and the lead group over-cooks the pace, leaving real closers with a genuine target.
scenarios.body: True hold-up types find a stronger tempo than anticipated has softened the leaders, and clean-jumping chasers positioned deep can pick up the pieces approaching the last; this depends on a shape this field is unlikely to produce given one genuine front-runner.

watchPoints.text: Jesse Evans — exceptional 15/15 Good-ground profile combined with a prominent style that directly suits this controlled pace; if he travels with his usual fluency, Sam Ewing will be hard to dislodge approaching the last.

Nowwhatdoyouthink — Jack Kennedy, 10/15 Good-ground form and a prominent style make him one of the most dangerous horses in the race if he settles behind Three Card Brag and jumps cleanly from the third-last.

Three Card Brag — lone front-runner with full control of the pace; watch how much Kevin Healy asks of him on the final circuit, because if he over-extends his lead, he could hold on, but a soft-pedal approach invites a wall of rivals turning in.

Reverend Hubert — exceptional Good-ground record (14/15) and red-hot current form; as a genuine hold-up type he needs something to go wrong up front, but if it does he is physically equipped to be the closest finisher from deep.

Boston Rover — three Good-ground wins from four is eye-catching but he is a prominent type forced deep in a 25-runner field just 19 days after his last run; watch his position early — if he can push forward he upgrades sharply, if not he becomes a spectator.

races.name: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden

runners_data.name: Believe Again
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a fading tendency flagged in recent runs, last seen 72 days ago, and sim-going record of 0 wins from 2 at this type of ground; needs a strong pace that this race shape may not deliver.

runners_data.name: Can Happen
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago which demands scrutiny; wears headgear and has 1 win from 10 similar-going runs, but the prominent style suits if she travels off a controlled pace set by Sunny South West.

runners_data.name: Coolnagrattan
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4-year-old with an unknown style profile; trainer in form at 1/2 over 14 days, and the 29-day freshener is a plus — unexposed enough to be interesting if the pace collapses.

runners_data.name: Daddy Long Legs
runners_data.note: Seasoned 7-year-old with four wins and eight places from 15 similar-going runs; Willie Mullins runner with Pat Mullins aboard and a strong record at 1m6f+ suggesting this 1m4f is on the short side but still within range.

runners_data.name: Eyeeye
runners_data.note: Trainer at 0/6 over 14 days and a form string of 5070/0 tells its own story; a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield map slot in this congested field, and the style-fit discount (0.91) combines with the fading tendency to make this a very tough winning proposition.

runners_data.name: Glowing Account
runners_data.note: Hasn't run in 943 days — the absence is the defining factor here; Mullins-trained and won on Good ground previously, but ring-rustiness over this trip in a 21-runner field is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Home By The Sea
runners_data.note: Consistent fader in finish with a 0W0P record on sim-going across three relevant runs; hold-up style and the flagged fade pattern make this a difficult winning proposition regardless of scenario.

runners_data.name: Hopes Are High
runners_data.note: 288-day layoff is significant; a natural prominent racer who won on Good and Soft ground, but being pushed into midfield by an overstocked pace group means he cannot race to his strengths without a trouble-free passage.

runners_data.name: Nakassama
runners_data.note: Has a smart record of 1W4P from 10 sim-going runs with strong efforts at extended trips; his natural prominent style is his asset but the crowded pace scenario means he is mapped out of position, requiring luck in running to fulfil that profile.

runners_data.name: Silas Marner
runners_data.note: 411 days off the track for the 9-year-old; showed ability at 19-20f trips earlier in career, and if this longer absence hasn't blunted that, he is a genuine hold-up type who benefits if the pace scenario C unfolds.

runners_data.name: Sunny South West
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner; record of 3W4P from 9 sim-going runs and an OR of 120 underlines the class — hg:h worn and the style-fit tag (0.91) is present but he IS the pace, so his position is secure regardless of field congestion.

runners_data.name: Kimy
runners_data.note: Fading tendency flagged; 0W2P record at Galway-type trips on Good, and the last run 22 days ago leaves enough freshness — but a midfield-to-rear runner who needs a true pace that may not come.

runners_data.name: Run For Mahler
runners_data.note: 3 wins and 6 places from 9 sim-going runs is an outstanding strike rate; prominent style suits perfectly and trainer at 1/6 over 14 days is encouraging — well-suited to the dominant scenario here.

runners_data.name: Abbotsford
runners_data.note: 3-year-old from the powerful Weld yard, carrying a lighter weight of 155lbs; just two runs in the book including a runner-up finish, and the prominent style could allow him to slot in off Sunny South West's pace.

runners_data.name: Chairmanforlife
runners_data.note: Lightly raced Harrington 3-year-old with an unknown tactical profile; trainer at 2/32 in the 14-day window and only two career runs, but Good ground form and the weight advantage (155lbs) keep him interesting.

runners_data.name: Mergus Serrator
runners_data.note: Unknown style type from Cromwell's yard; trainer at 2/38 in the 14-day window but the 3-year-old has consistent placed efforts including a fourth on Good — could find a position if the race falls apart.

runners_data.name: New Bay Star
runners_data.note: Three consecutive runner-up finishes on Tapeta/Soft; first run on Good turf is a significant unknown — hold-up style but the going switch is a genuine query for Michael Appleby's raider.

runners_data.name: Will You Stop
runners_data.note: 3-year-old with three runs all on Good ground at shorter trips; prominent style and the lighter weight (155lbs) are in his favour, but stepping up sharply in trip to 1m4f from 10f is unproven.

runners_data.name: Galileo Springs
runners_data.note: 1W5P record from 10 sim-going runs is solid; prominent style suits the expected race shape and the trainer at 0/0 in the 14-day window is neutral — worth noting the horse won at 17f suggesting stamina is not an issue.

runners_data.name: It's Good To Talk
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a fading tendency; 58 days off and an OR of 120 but sim-going record of 0W0P from three relevant runs — needs a strong pace to close into and the scenario for this type is the least likely here.

runners_data.name: Four Ball
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3-year-old from Murphy's yard with just one run; unknown style, trainer at 1/10 over 14 days, and the single run on Good gives minimal evidence — purely speculative at this stage.

races.paceDynamic: Sunny South West is the confirmed lone front-runner in a 21-runner maiden at 1m4f on Good ground at Galway, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout. The field contains an unusually heavy concentration of prominent-style horses — Can Happen, Daddy Long Legs, Glowing Account, Run For Mahler, Abbotsford, Will You Stop, Galileo Springs, and Chairmanforlife all want to race prominently — meaning several will be shuffled back from their natural positions and race in an uncharacteristic role. Nakassama and Hopes Are High are genuine prominent types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the race shape simply cannot accommodate them all at the head of affairs. With Sunny South West able to control tempo unchallenged and the pace strung out through the first half, hold-up horses will need a strong pace injection that may not materialise, leaving horses with natural gate-to-wire or prominent tactical speed best placed; the race shape strongly favours prominent racers who secure a position close to the controlled pace and have the class or stamina to sustain their effort through the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sunny South West Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sunny South West secures the lead unchallenged and sets a measured, even gallop that suits horses racing prominently in a compressed bunch.
scenarios.body: Sunny South West dictates from the front and the moderate tempo compresses the field, meaning prominent horses who travel sweetly and finish straight benefit most as no one can close from deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Finishes Strong
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched prominent group races as a unit and the pace is just fast enough to stretch out hold-up types, producing a finish between the front three or four.
scenarios.body: The even pace allows several prominent horses to travel in a tight group through the straight, and the lack of a late burst from hold-up types means the winner emerges from those who tracked the leader throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the compact prominent field sets a stronger-than-expected tempo in the early and middle stages, leaving the front runners exposed in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A faster early gallop burns off the prominent horses and opens a gap for genuine hold-up types to reel in tiring leaders, though note that several mapped hold-up types here are natural prominent racers displaced rearward, which reduces this scenario's reliability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses fight for position early and produce a falsely fast first half that results in widespread tiring in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A chaotic tempo surge in a field of 21 leaves many frontrunners spent, opening the race to horses with an ability to pick up off a fast pace, including lightly raced unexposed types.

watchPoints.text: Sunny South West's ability to get a clear lead unchallenged is the single most important factor — if he is harassed for the pace by any of the prominent group (Can Happen, Glowing Account, Will You Stop), the entire pace dynamic changes and the dominant scenario loses validity.

Nakassama and Hopes Are High are both genuine prominent types mapped to midfield due to field congestion — watch whether either secures an early position closer to the pace than their map slot suggests, as both carry strong place form on similar going.

Glowing Account returns from a 943-day absence for Mullins — an unusually long layoff in a 21-runner maiden; if freshened perfectly she has the talent, but the absence risk is real and worth monitoring in the market.

The weight advantage held by 3-year-olds (155lbs vs 161-166lbs for older horses) across Abbotsford, Chairmanforlife, Mergus Serrator, New Bay Star, Will You Stop, and Four Ball could be significant in a stamina test over 1m4f on Good ground — watch if any 3-year-old drifts or shortens dramatically before the off.

Run For Mahler's sim-going record of 3W6P from 9 runs is the standout strike rate in the field — if the Byrnes runner is prominently supported in the market, it would align directly with the dominant race shape.

races.name: Tote Every Day Is A Money-Back Day Handicap

runners_data.name: Mayflower
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who controlled a mile maiden at Sandown last time out; 66 days off is worth noting, and her form before that win was moderate (three consecutive sixes), so the question is whether she can reproduce that winning effort over an extra trip after a break — her natural pace-setting role is genuine here.

runners_data.name: Moonlit Sun
runners_data.note: Ran a solid second at Galway over a mile just 35 days ago then came home first last time, accumulating a 2/2 record at the track on Good — the combination of course form, a top-class conditional booking in Shane Foley and a prominent style that suits this shape makes her a natural fit.

runners_data.name: God Of Power
runners_data.note: Three wins from starts over seven and eight furlongs on Good, trained and ridden by Andrew Slattery who is operating at 5/35 in the past fortnight; steps up in trip slightly but his prominent racing style is suited to the expected pace shape.

runners_data.name: Kirkland Sioux
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back over a mile on Good and returns just ten days after his last run for the in-form Joseph O'Brien team (19/68 in 14 days); the quick reappearance at the same track where he has won twice recently is a positive flag, and he holds a natural position tracking the pace.

runners_data.name: Amenita
runners_data.note: Won impressively over a mile on Good for Dermot Weld last time; a genuinely prominent-profile horse who figures to be shuffled back given the headcount ahead of her, and her chance is shaped by whether she can overcome a drawn position and reclaim her natural pitch — Reese Holohan claims 7lb.

runners_data.name: Johnny Soda
runners_data.note: Back-to-back mile wins on Good, with his trainer Adrian McGuinness running at 2/26 in the past fortnight; a prominent racer who is well-placed in this shape and has clearly taken to the mile trip, though stepping up to a mile and a half is a new question.

runners_data.name: Krasimir
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse who has hit the frame in six of seven starts on Good ground — his natural style is prominent but the size of this field pushes him into a position he won't naturally seek, and the tongue-tie is worth noting; his record shows durability rather than a strong finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Monvoe
runners_data.note: Three wins from Good ground over a mile, but his last run saw him beaten into ninth over nine furlongs on Good — his form suggests he is at his best over the shorter end of this trip, and being displaced from his natural prominent pitch is a concern at this longer distance.

runners_data.name: Time Bender
runners_data.note: Won over seven furlongs on Good but his three subsequent runs have all yielded sixths or worse; a prominent racer by nature whose map position does not reflect where he wants to be, and he needs to find significant improvement over a trip he has not yet won at.

runners_data.name: Loch Gamhna
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a best recent effort of third over twelve furlongs on Good — that stamina profile is relevant at a mile and a half, but his form string of 78673 suggests he is struggling to compete at this level; Paddy Harnett claims 5lb.

runners_data.name: Monoceros
runners_data.note: Placed in three of five Good-ground starts and brings course form from a recent run; a true hold-up horse whose pattern is to close late, and if the pace scenario obliges he is the more credible of the two closers — Iain Jardine has been busy (3/22) and Ronan Whelan is a strong booking.

runners_data.name: Minella Rockett
runners_data.note: Won over sixteen furlongs on Good, so the stamina is not in doubt, but he is a prominent-profile horse who will struggle to secure his preferred position with this field; his drop back in trip to a mile and a half from those longer efforts is noteworthy, though he has shown ability at shorter distances.

runners_data.name: Golddream
runners_data.note: Won over a mile on Soft/Heavy for David Marnane and has since posted a run of 61355; a prominent-style horse by nature who will be shuffled toward midfield by the competitive early pace, and his Good-ground strike rate of 0/5 is a concern on today's going.

races.paceDynamic: Mayflower is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner handicap over a mile and a half at Galway, and with no genuine pressure expected, she should be able to dictate a sustainable, even gallop from the front. Behind her, Kirkland Sioux, Moonlit Sun, God Of Power and Johnny Soda are the next most likely to occupy the early prominent positions, with genuine competition for those berths ensuring the tempo is not crawlingly slow. This field is overloaded with prominent-profile runners — Amenita, Krasimir, Monvoe, Time Bender, Minella Rockett and Golddream are all natural prominent types who cannot all get their preferred position and will be shuffled back, diluting the effectiveness of the hold-up contingent (Loch Gamhna, Monoceros) whose finishing runs will be launched into a field that never really strung out. With a lone front-runner setting a manageable gallop on Good ground, this race shape most strongly favours horses that can race prominently in the first four or five, travel without cover and deliver a sustained finish from a controlled position — true prominent types with course/going form and the tactical awareness to seize their ground early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mayflower Controls, Chasers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Mayflower dictates a steady, uncontested lead and the main prominent chasers track closely before the turn for home.
scenarios.body: Mayflower sets an honest but manageable gallop and the horses who travel just behind her — Kirkland Sioux, Moonlit Sun, Johnny Soda — are best placed to respond when the race quickens turning in on Good ground; the distance of a mile and a half on a flat circuit rewards horses who can hold a prominent pitch without burning out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Overcrowding Sparks Pace
scenarios.trigger: If competition for the early prominent positions forces a stronger-than-expected gallop and the race becomes a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: Several prominent-profile horses pressing for position in the first half-mile lift the pace beyond what Mayflower wants, turning this into a proper gallop that sifts out the stayers; at a mile and a half on Good ground, this scenario favours horses with proven stamina and the ability to rattle home from off a genuine pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Runners Unleashed Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to leave the closers with a wall of tiring horses to pick through in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Loch Gamhna and Monoceros are genuine hold-up types who can finish strongly if the gallop has been searching; however, with so many redistributed prominent horses filling the midfield, the closing run may be blocked until too late on a flat track that rarely suits wide or late challengers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Chaos Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Mayflower is swamped early by multiple rivals vying for position and the race deteriorates into a messy, stop-start contest.
scenarios.body: A chaotic race with no clear early order can randomise the outcome, handing an advantage to a horse that flukes a perfect trip through the melee; however, this is the least likely shape given Mayflower's clear front-running profile and the overall competitive but not explosive nature of this field.

watchPoints.text: Kirkland Sioux has won twice at Galway over a mile on Good in recent weeks and returns after just ten days for a red-hot trainer — watch whether he sits just off Mayflower's heels and delivers his challenge from a position of maximum advantage.

The sheer volume of prominent-profile horses vying for early position — particularly Amenita, Monvoe, Krasimir and Johnny Soda — could lift the gallop beyond what Mayflower wants to set, fundamentally altering the race shape; watch the first two furlongs closely.

Moonlit Sun's two Galway wins (including one over this course) make her a significant danger if she travels comfortably in the first four — watch whether Shane Foley places her just behind the pace or gets outmanoeuvred at the start.

Monoceros is the most credible of the hold-up runners if the pace scenario develops strongly enough; watch whether Ronan Whelan angles for a clear run on the outside from the three-furlong pole, as a blocked passage on the flat Galway track would likely end his chance.

Mayflower has not run for 66 days and won for the first time last time out — watch her demeanour in the paddock and how quickly she establishes her lead, as any hesitation from the gate could see her swamped by the prominent cluster before the race settles.

runners_data.name: Rock Of Ireland

runners_data.name: Sea Eagle

runners_data.name: Black Heather

runners_data.name: Ben Hur
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer who cannot get his natural position in this 23-runner field; the 215-day layoff is an enormous flag and Noel Meade's T14 is modest (3/13) — even if fitness is there, the style displacement and absence combine to make this a speculative interest at best.

races.paceDynamic: Rock Of Ireland is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse setting the pace in a 23-runner field over 2m½f on Good ground, the tempo figures to be controlled and sustainable rather than punishing. Gaoth Chuil, Wackestone, Liam Swagger, Sign From Above, Louiescall, Slurricane and Boxing Great are all genuine prominent types who will want to sit close to the pace, but in a field this large only a handful can realistically secure that early position — Gaoth Chuil (in-form, course winner) and Wackestone (Gordon Elliott booking) are likeliest to occupy the primary prominent slots, with others shuffled wider or further back than their natural style. Ben Hur is a true prominent racer redistributed to midfield on the map because the space in front simply does not exist; similarly, Rakki, Wahraan, Forlio, Papagei and Harry's Legacy are natural hold-up horses pushed to a midfield designation that flatters their ability to sustain a challenge from off the pace. A single uncontested front-runner setting a measured gallop over an extended trip on Good ground is a textbook recipe for the race to be run at a fair but not excessive pace, which keeps the front rank in the race longer and favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and have the stamina to press in the straight — hold-up horses will need an unusually strong final-quarter gallop to get involved.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Front Suits
scenarios.trigger: If Rock Of Ireland leads at a measured gallop and the prominent group travels well within themselves into the straight.
scenarios.body: Rock Of Ireland sets a fair clip unchallenged, allowing the prominent horses immediately behind — Gaoth Chuil and Wackestone in particular — to travel sweetly and strike early in the Galway straight where there is no room for hold-up horses to weave through a bunched field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is modest enough that several prominent racers surge simultaneously from the home turn and overwhelm the leader.
scenarios.body: Rock Of Ireland's controlled gallop sets up a fast-finishing final quarter for those just off the pace, and horses like Louiescall, Liam Swagger and Sign From Above who have the stamina for this trip pounce in a group finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and creates sufficient stop-start fractions to bring the genuine hold-up horses into play.
scenarios.body: Black Heather and Cock And Bull, both consistent hold-up performers with solid Good-ground records, can sustain runs from well off the pace if the leaders tire in the final furlong; Not Just Any Eagle is also capable on her day at this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Rock Of Ireland bowls along unchallenged and the prominent pack behind burns each other out scrapping for position.
scenarios.body: With 23 runners jostling for early prominent slots, the horses immediately behind Rock Of Ireland may use energy disputing position, leaving the leader clear to steal a decisive break and simply stay on; Eastmore's consistent top-three finishing habit on Good ground suits a rail-skimming gallop.

watchPoints.text: Gaoth Chuil has two recent wins on Good ground at this trip range and will push forward to sit just behind Rock Of Ireland — watch for him to quicken earliest once the leader is challenged in the straight.

With 23 runners, the break from the gates will determine a great deal; watch for Wackestone, Liam Swagger and Louiescall to fight for the prominent positions and any who get shuffled wide or back will be racing out of their ideal shape.

Rock Of Ireland's 87-day layoff means fitness must be questioned despite his tactical advantage as sole front-runner — if he weakens inside the final quarter-mile the race could collapse into a heap finish where any of the prominent pack land.

Eastmore's exceptional Good-ground profile (sim-going 14/15) with no jockey currently declared is worth monitoring — a top booking confirmed late would sharply upgrade the case for a front-rank racer whose flat-finish stamina record is the strongest in the field.
